payload.key: "a built revision is hashed and drift is detectable" changed since you answered "leave it: review status reads the bundle and its artifact hashes without changing how they are built or verified" to "does review status change what the built-revision hashing says?". does your answer still hold for what it says now? then: build-application renders the policy-selected documents into a new revision directory, runs the checks and writes bundle.json with the sha-256 of every selected input, package asset and artifact; verify-bundle recomputes them and reports changed or missing entries. ex-1: given a valid application, when cv build-application runs into a new revision directory, then bundle.json lists every input and artifact with its hash and the checks results ex-2: given a bundle whose resume source changed after the build, when cv verify-bundle runs, then the changed path is reported and the status is not ok now: build-application renders the policy-selected documents into a new revision directory, runs the checks and writes bundle.json with the sha-256 of every selected input, package asset and artifact, except the editable resume.md and cover-letter.md copies at the revision's top; verify-bundle recomputes them and reports changed or missing entries. ex-1: given a valid application, when cv build-application runs into a new revision directory, then bundle.json lists every input and artifact with its hash and the checks results ex-2: given a bundle whose resume source changed after the build, when cv verify-bundle runs, then the changed path is reported and the status is not ok what changed: dec-007 says to leave the way bundle hashes are built and verified alone, but sr-005 now exempts the editable resume.md and cover-letter.md copies from bundle.json hashing, so it no longer covers every artifact. it comes from your decision "does review status change what the built-revision hashing says?" of 2026-11-16.
